_comment: Task 12 listening render 1/3 (task-12-brief-addendum.md section C). BODY on part A, STEP plucking every ~2s. SOURCE (slot 0) is MATL here, swept 0 -> 0.5 -> 1.0 across three 8 s sections: plucked harp (string-dominant) -> prepared piano (blend) -> struck bells (modal-dominant). This is NOT a four-note chord strum: BodyVoice::kEngineVoices == 1, so trigger_chord keeps only the root (synth_engine.cpp's n > kVoices clamp). What COLOR does here is move the chord's QUALITY the layer would have voiced -- read as chord_character and used to bend the mode bank's inharmonicity direction (spec section 5/section 7 amendment 2) -- so the material sweep is real even though only one note ever sounds. DETUNE is left nonzero on purpose: at DETUNE = 0 the stretch product is zero and COLOR's bend is inaudible (section 7 amendment 2), which would make this scenario silently fail to demonstrate the thing its own COLOR events claim to move.

init._comment: Part B silenced: default lanes would otherwise siren its own pitch.
Exciter: short click, moderate ring -- a pluck, not a bow.

SUB (excitation bus level) left at 0: this scenario is about MATL and chord quality, not the excitation bus -- SUB = 0 hard-gates that whole path (spec section 6), which keeps this render free of a second variable.

LEVEL pinned high and steady, for a deterministic non-modulated level. Note for the listening pass: this did NOT raise the peak (still ~-24 dBFS/0.056 -- checked while building this render) -- LEVEL is not what is quiet here, the click-zone pluck patch itself (ATTACK .05 / DECAY .55 / RESO .1) is just intrinsically low-output relative to body_bow's continuous exciter. Worth knowing before judging the MATL sweep by ear: turn the monitor up rather than assume this scenario failed to trigger.

events._comment: 0-8s: plucked harp -- string-dominant, near-harmonic (COLOR at minimum is the base stretch direction, spec section 7 amendment 2).
8-16s: prepared piano -- string/modal blend, chord quality bending toward a more broken ratio.
16-24s: struck bells -- modal-dominant, most-stretched chord quality.
